races.title: State Assembly, District 61
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Tina Simone McKinnor
cands.bio: Democrat who has served in the California State Assembly since December 2022, representing District 61. Earlier worked as an auditor for the Los Angeles County Office of Education, a political treasurer, an Assembly chief of staff, operations director for the California Democratic Party, and civic engagement director of LAVoice.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists 2026 endorsements from the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions AFL-CIO, California Teachers Association, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, California Young Democrats, Equality California and YIMBY Action.

cands.gaps: We found no documented deeds or stated positions from her on data centers, property taxes, institutional or foreign land buyers, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, police and public order, guns, abortion, or school choice. She did not complete Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey in 2022, 2024 or 2026, so we have no questionnaire answers. We could not establish where she was raised or when she may have moved within California. We found no reporting on controversies, and no foreign ties. The Ballotpedia page lists bills she sponsored but the list was empty in the text we could read.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia says she was born in Los Angeles County and shows her studying at Los Angeles Southwest College in 2003 and working in California for years since, but her upbringing is not documented.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assembly member since December 2022, after serving as an Assembly chief of staff. Earlier she was an auditor for the Los Angeles County Office of Education and a political treasurer, and she holds a B.A. in accounting and an A.A. in business administration and accounting. She is listed as a small business owner.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service and staff experience in the chamber, plus an accounting and audit career relevant to budget work. Committee chairing was not counted.

cands.name: Brian Lockwood
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California State Assembly District 61 (Los Angeles). Works in finance and property management. Past Grand Knight of Knights of Columbus Council #3744, former Westchester/Playa Neighborhood Council director, and Communications Director of the Republican Party of Los Angeles County.

endorsements.text: Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (Sway voting group) listed him as a recommendation.

cands.gaps: His birthplace, where he grew up, and when he came to California are not documented; the only evidence is his own description of himself as a 6th-generation Los Angeleno. We found no prior elected office beyond a neighborhood council seat, and no employer names or dates for his finance and property management work. We found no documented actions in office, and no statements on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buying, growth and land protection, H-1B or immigration enforcement, gun policy, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site and survey speak only in general terms about cutting 'restrictive taxes & red tape,' with no specifics. No controversies, foreign ties, or notable endorsements beyond one voter guide turned up in the pages we had.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Career in finance and property management; former Residential Director on the Westchester/Playa Neighborhood Council; Communications Director of the Los Angeles County Republican Party. He has held no legislative office.
qual.why: Private-sector work in finance and property management fits the middle band. He has no legislative, policy or budget career. Neighborhood council and party roles are civic or party posts and add nothing to the score.
